pageCache.pageTitle: Elham Church of England Primary School - MFL French
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Elham Church of England Primary School
MFL French
MFL French
Intent
At Elham School, the intent of the French (MFL) curriculum is to inspire curiosity and a positive attitude towards language learning while developing pupils’ confidence and faith in their own ability to succeed. We aim to provide a high-quality language education that supports achievement and fosters an understanding of the French language and culture, laying strong foundations for further language learning at secondary school. Through engaging and age-appropriate lessons, pupils develop speaking, listening, reading and writing skills alongside key grammatical knowledge, enabling them to communicate meaningfully beyond their immediate environment. Our curriculum promotes empathy, inclusivity and cultural awareness, helping pupils understand their role within local, national and global communities and recognise the importance of language in building connections, mutual respect and understanding across cultures.
Implementation
French is taught using the Language Angels scheme of work, which provides a progressive and structured approach to language learning. In Key Stage 2, pupils in Years 3–6 follow a two-year rolling programme to ensure continuity, progression and full coverage of the National Curriculum. Lessons are carefully sequenced to build knowledge and skills in speaking, listening, reading and writing, with grammar introduced and revisited in a clear and age-appropriate way. Language Angels’ units support teachers with high-quality resources, including interactive activities, songs, stories and assessment tools, enabling consistent delivery across the school.
In Key Stage 1, pupils are introduced to French through informal and engaging activities such as singing songs, learning basic greetings and numbers, and responding to simple words and phrases. This early exposure develops pupils’ listening skills, confidence and enthusiasm for language learning, preparing them for more formal French lessons in Key Stage 2. Throughout the school, opportunities are provided for pupils to practise pronunciation, develop cultural awareness and use language in meaningful contexts.
Impact
The impact of our French (MFL) curriculum is that pupils develop a secure foundation in basic French language skills and are able to communicate ideas with increasing confidence and accuracy. They demonstrate enthusiasm for language learning, a willingness to participate in spoken activities, and an awareness of French culture and traditions. By the end of Key Stage 2, pupils are able to understand and respond to simple spoken and written French, write short sentences using familiar vocabulary, and apply basic grammar rules. This ensures they are well prepared for the transition to secondary education and equipped with the skills, knowledge and attitudes needed to continue learning languages successfully.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Elham Church of England Primary School
PE & Sports Premium
PE & Sports Premium
School Games Mark
We are proud to have achieved the School Games Gold Mark for the last four consecutive years. This government-led award, delivered by the Youth Sport Trust, recognises schools for their commitment to providing high-quality competitive sport both within school and across the wider community.
What is the PE and Sport Premium?
The Government provides additional funding to primary schools to improve the quality of physical education (PE), physical activity and sport for all pupils. This funding is jointly provided by the Departments for Education, Health and Culture, Media and Sport, and is allocated directly to primary school headteachers to enhance PE and sporting opportunities.
Purpose of the Funding
Schools have the flexibility to decide how best to use the PE and Sport Premium to improve the quality of their PE and sport provision.
At Elham Church of England Primary School, we recognise the vital role that PE and sport play in promoting children's physical health, mental wellbeing and personal development. We believe that a broad and varied PE curriculum, alongside a wide range of extra-curricular sporting opportunities, encourages positive attitudes towards healthy lifestyles, builds confidence and resilience, and supports children's academic achievement.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Elham Church of England Primary School
Our Church School
Church Explorers
Church Explorers
Church Explorers meets in St Mary's Church on the third Tuesday of each month between 3:30 and 4:30 p.m. This club provides a fun way for children aged 7-11 to explore the Bible, prayer, and the Christian faith in the church. It is led by Rev Carol, along with other village members who are all DBS-checked. They organise games, crafts, music, activities, and plenty of cake!
Let Mrs Lewis know if you would like to come!
Church Explorers are exploring textures in Saint Mary's Church with rubbings.

Welcome to Elham Church of England Primary School
PSHE & RSE
PSHE & RSE
Progression-of-Knowledge and Skills PSHE.RSE.pdf PDF File
Intent
At Elham Church of England Primary School, our Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) and Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) curriculum is designed to support pupils in becoming healthy, confident, respectful and responsible individuals. Rooted in our Christian values of faith, achievement, community and empathy, our curriculum promotes pupils’ spiritual, moral, social and cultural development and prepares them for life in modern Britain.
Our intent is to equip pupils with the knowledge, skills and understanding they need to:
Build positive, respectful and healthy relationships
Understand and manage their physical and emotional well-being
Develop a strong sense of identity, self-worth and resilience
Make informed, age-appropriate choices
Respect diversity and show empathy towards others
PSHE and RSE are delivered in line with statutory guidance for Relationships Education, Relationships and Sex Education and Health Education, ensuring content is age-appropriate, inclusive and sensitive. Teaching reflects the Church of England’s vision of enabling all pupils to flourish and live life in all its fullness, while recognising and respecting the beliefs, values and backgrounds of all families within our school community.
Implementation
PSHE and RSE are taught using the Kapow Primary PSHE and RSE Scheme of Learning, which provides a coherent, spiral curriculum that builds knowledge, skills and understanding progressively from Early Years to Year 6.
The curriculum is organised into key strands, including:
Families and relationships
Health and well-being
Safety and the changing body (RSE)
Lessons are taught in a safe, supportive and respectful environment where pupils are encouraged to ask questions, share ideas and reflect thoughtfully. Clear ground rules are established to ensure discussions are handled sensitively and inclusively.
Our school values are embedded throughout:
Faith supports moral development, reflection and understanding of right and wrong.
Achievement is promoted through goal-setting, resilience and positive self-belief.
Community is developed through learning about belonging, democracy, respect and responsibility.
Empathy underpins learning about relationships, diversity, inclusion and emotional well-being.
RSE content is taught in an age-appropriate manner, focusing on relationships, respect, body awareness, personal safety and emotional changes, with statutory sex education taught in Year 6 in line with guidance and parental consultation. Parents are informed about RSE content and have the right to withdraw their child from non-statutory elements.
PSHE and RSE are further enhanced through collective worship, themed days, pupil voice opportunities and links to safeguarding and pastoral support.
Impact
As a result of our PSHE and RSE curriculum, pupils at Elham Church of England Primary School:
Show confidence in understanding themselves and managing their emotions
Form and maintain positive, respectful relationships
Demonstrate empathy, kindness and respect for diversity
Make informed choices that support their physical and mental health
Understand how to keep themselves and others safe
Pupils leave our school well-prepared for the next stage of their education and for life beyond primary school. They are equipped with the personal, social and emotional skills needed to thrive as responsible members of their community, living out our Christian values in their daily lives.

forest-school-learning
We are very proud to be able to offer Forest School Learning for the children at our school. With help from The Big Lottery we have been able to build a roundhouse and purchase the resources and training to ensure that this is done well.
A Forest School (FS) Handbook for Elham Church of England Primary School has been compiled to outline the policies and procedures that are in place to keep everyone involved in our FS safe.
This handbook has been written alongside other school policies and procedures and these should be read in conjunction with this document. The handbook will be read by all adults who have a regular role in FS learning. The handbook is a working document and will be reviewed regularly and at least annually.
